title: 'Screentime to cash' scam-PSA wave on #screentime
summary: Several unrelated accounts post PSA warnings or 'has anyone joined this program?' confessions about screen-time-to-cash reward offers. #tiktokprogam showed 87 posts logged out; #screentime is dominated by this format; sampled posts all from the last ~10 days (earliest 10-1).
hook_text: Do not assume this is TikTok!
why_it_works: Money plus a scam warning tied to screen time: viewers share it to protect friends (shares near or above likes), and the 'program' sounds official.
use_for_us: An App Island beat where a shady contestant offers 'cash for your screen time' and the others call it out, hinting at the scam without naming any real app.
format: green-screen PSA, talking head, fake offer card

title: 'Screentime to cash is NOT TikTok!' PSA, 43.1K likes vs ~36 normal
summary: Creator talks to camera over a green-screen PSA frame warning about a 'screentime to cash' offer. Posted 10-1 (as shown). Huge outlier: the account's other posts show 36 and 6 likes.
hook_text: Do not assume this is TikTok!
why_it_works: Opens with a direct warning that contradicts what viewers assume; protective-share trigger drives 24.8K shares.
use_for_us: Open an episode on a bold on-screen warning line that flips an assumption about an app character.

title: Low-effort 'has anyone joined this program?' selfie, ~40x account norm
summary: Plain selfie talking head asking whether anyone joined the screen-time cash program, captioned 'Has anyone joined this program or am I about to get haaaaaacked?'. Posted 10-1; her other posts show 6-14 likes.
hook_text: Has this happened to anyone else?
why_it_works: A question hook that invites comments (85 comments on 406 likes); viewers answer from their own experience.
use_for_us: End an episode with a 'has this happened to anyone else?' style question to pull relatable comments.

title: AI 3D fruit-character skit, 32.6K likes in 19h

why_it_works: Cute object characters in a mundane human situation; AI label did not stop reach, and saves (5567) show rewatch value.
use_for_us: Confirms AI-labeled 3D object-character skits can scale; put our app characters in everyday human situations and track @funwithfruit as a benchmark.

use_for_us: Watch-list benchmark for App Island: recurring cast, episode cadence, hook styles.

title: Calmlings (Calm Studios): AI 3D cute-creature brand, 0 to 2B+ views in 10 months, $0 ad spend
summary: Owned by Calm (meditation app) via in-house Calm Studios; started Aug 2025. Fully AI-made (Nano Banana images + Veo video, Gemini multi-agent system mines their own analytics to plan and storyboard), ~1-2 videos/day cross-posted to FB (3.78M followers), IG (1M), TikTok (930.7K), YouTube (12.4K, weak). Monetizes via brand deals (e.g. TRIP drinks: 3 posts 8.1M views in 3 weeks) and an upcoming care-for-a-Calmling game; never pushes the Calm app in posts.
hook_text: I was gonna clean my house
why_it_works: One soft, consistent mascot world (Calm Island) + everyday-tired relatable lines (back pain, coffee, no sleep, procrastination, doomscrolling) + send-this-to-someone captions; high volume daily posting lets the algorithm find 1M+ hits daily (their claim). Parent brand is invisible, so it reads as entertainment not ads. Audience skews 78% women, 25-54, US 51%.
use_for_us: Validates our play: keep EndScroll nearly invisible, build a recurring character world, use first-person relatable hooks and share/tag captions; their gap is younger 16-28 and the scroll-as-villain angle, which App Island can own. Volume matters: they post daily, we post every 2 days.
format: AI 3D cute mascot micro-clips (9-20s), single scene, text overlay
sound: Original audio; also parody songs (21M-view TikTok was a my-lower-back-hurts parody song)

title: Calmlings doomscroll reel: I was gonna work out / but I grabbed my phone

why_it_works: Rhymed sing-song lyric structure (I was gonna... / But I grabbed my phone) turns a guilty habit into a cute confession; viewers recognise the exact moment of failure.
use_for_us: Direct template for App Island: a contestant (Scroll) sings the I-was-gonna / but-I-grabbed-my-phone lyric; one intention, one phone grab, one couch ending.

title: Tiny 4-sub channel hits 9.4K views with 11s 'I'm addicted to my phone' expectation-vs-reality cartoon
summary: 2D AI-looking stick-figure character in a bedroom; opens on the weekend plans it wants (yoga, books, travel), and the reality is presumably lying on the phone. Only the opening second was confirmed.
hook_text: My plans for the weekend: 🧘📚✈️
why_it_works: Expectation-vs-reality setup in the first frame: viewers instantly predict the phone punchline and see themselves; 11s length makes it loop.
use_for_us: Open an App Island episode with the viewer's 'plans' card, then cut to the apps fighting to wreck them.

title: 'Daily Routine (Phone Addiction)' cartoon: 4.5K views on a 108-sub channel
summary: Cartoon man brushes his teeth while scrolling his phone on the stairs; a daily-routine montage where the phone is in every task.
hook_text: Daily Routine 😂
why_it_works: Specific mundane moments (brushing teeth while scrolling) give viewers the 'that's literally me' jolt; ~40x subscriber count suggests the feed is pushing it.
use_for_us: Use concrete everyday moments (toothbrush, stairs) as the 'dates' where apps compete for the viewer.

title: 'Which app is your favorite?' skit with an in-video app poll sticker
summary: Live-action 7s lip-sync skit on which app is best, with a YouTube poll sticker (Instagram / Snapchat / TikTok / YouTube). Modest views for a 21K channel (1.7K).
hook_text: Which App is your favourite?
why_it_works: Asks the viewer to pick a side, which pulls comments and votes; the poll sticker turns a 7s clip into an interaction.
use_for_us: Our Ep2 'who stays' vote could use an on-screen poll prompt (with hinted, unnamed apps) instead of relying only on the comment.
format: live-action lip-sync skit with poll sticker

summary: Unrelated accounts (Laughs After Work, Laugh Line USA, others) post cartoons where the weekly Screen Time report is a character that roasts the owner. Views are still tiny (2-15), so this is an early copied format, not a hit.

why_it_works: Turns a dreaded notification into a character with attitude; easy, repeatable joke structure.
use_for_us: A 'Screen Time report' host or judge character on App Island who reads out the weekly totals at elimination.

title: Anti-doomscroll apps are marketing with cheap POV/anime Shorts (ScrollToll, Step N Scroll)
summary: New small channels post doomscroll POV clips that plug lock-your-phone apps: anime boy morning routine (ScrollToll, ~1K views) and 'pov: running to erase 6 hours of screen time guilt' (Step N Scroll, 1.1K views on 32 subs).
hook_text: Get up.
why_it_works: POV guilt hooks ('6 hours of screen time guilt') land; the app plug is right in the description.
use_for_us: Competitors push the app hard; our edge is staying funny and barely mentioning EndScroll. Watch these as the competitor set.
format: POV / anime motivational clip with app promo

title: Revenge bedtime procrastination confession: 'stealing time from my own sleep and calling it self-care'
summary: First-person post about finally getting free time at 10pm, telling yourself you earned it, then staying up till 1am watching random stuff you don't even enjoy. 255 replies, many echoing 'revenge bedtime procrastination is real' (some replies look like engagement-farm accounts).
hook_text: I was stealing time from my own sleep and calling it self-care.
why_it_works: Self-aware confession with a twist: the 'reward' is something you don't even enjoy. Viewers recognise the 10pm 'I deserve this' bargain instantly.
use_for_us: An App Island beat where the feed app woos YOU at 10pm with 'you earned this' and the date ends at 1am with nothing you liked. Blames the design, not the viewer.

title: 'Itching to delete every app, I need a dopamine detox' - recurring casual complaint
summary: Short relatable complaint with several near-identical posts the same day (e.g. 'I really think I need a dopamine detox at this point'). The 'dopamine detox' wish is being voiced casually by young users, not as self-help.
hook_text: Itching to delete every app, I need a dopamine detox
why_it_works: Low-effort, half-joking admission that many people echo; it is the 'half-know they scroll too much' feeling in one line.
use_for_us: Opening line or on-screen text: a contestant app panics when the viewer says 'I need a dopamine detox'. Keeps it funny, not preachy.

title: News: parents fear YouTubers are bringing 'brain rot' to Netflix (The Guardian)
summary: News share of a Guardian Technology story about a polarising YouTube-style kids' show arriving on Netflix and parents calling it 'brain rot'. Other posts frame it as fast-paced videos and nonstop challenges built to keep kids watching.
hook_text: Parents fear YouTubers are bringing 'brain rot' to Netflix. But are kids wising up to 'slop'?
why_it_works: Cultural moment around 'brain rot' and 'slop' as everyday words; reaction window is short.
use_for_us: Possible 48h reaction angle: 'brain rot' moving from phones to the TV. Must avoid naming real companies or making factual claims about them (red line); audience fit is weaker since the story is about kids/parents.

title: Calmlings: I was gonna clean my house (doomscroll, 5.1M views)
summary: A pink fluffy 3D creature holding a broom and cleaning bottles in a cozy cabin; the plan to clean collapses because she doomscrolls instead. Caption: her brain is blown from doomscrolling. Sibling of the already-logged 'I was gonna work out / but I grabbed my phone'.
hook_text: I was gonna clean my house
why_it_works: Names a tiny, universal good intention in the first frame, so the viewer already knows the phone will win and feels caught; cute creature makes the self-mockery soft, no guilt.
use_for_us: An App Island cold open where YOU announce one plan ('I was gonna clean my room') and the contestants instantly start competing to derail it.

title: 'I was gonna ___' intention-then-phone setup copied across accounts
summary: The 'I was gonna [do a good thing]' opener appears in two Calmlings hits (work out; clean my house) and is echoed by small creators, e.g. a personal post 'i was just gonna scroll on TikTok for a few minutes and now i'm sprinting...'. Evidence for copying beyond Calmlings is weak (small accounts only).
hook_text: I was gonna clean my house
why_it_works: A one-line plan sets up an instant, predictable reversal; the viewer fills in the punchline ('...and then I picked up my phone') themselves.
use_for_us: Use 'I was gonna ___' as the first on-screen line of an episode; each episode swaps the plan (sleep, homework, gym).

title: Sharny & Julius: your teenager isn't addicted to the screen, they're addicted to escape
summary: A man talks to camera in a field with bold yellow text overlays reframing teen screen addiction as escape from a boring, lonely or heavy real life. Aimed at parents rather than 16-28 viewers.

why_it_works: Contrarian reframe ('it's not X, it's Y') in the first line; high share count (1.9K) relative to comments suggests people forward it to someone.
use_for_us: A contestant could pitch itself as 'the escape' rather than 'the app' - a reframe line the host can say plainly.

use_for_us: Episode idea: the viewer picks up a book and the app contestants try to win them back mid-page; target the self-improvement crowd.

title: 4-sub channel's animated 'Phone Addiction Made Him Miss This' short: 1.2K views in 16h
summary: A 30-second stylized animated short: a pale round character alone on a dark street by a lit window, about phone addiction making him miss something. The channel has 4 subscribers and 4 videos.

title: Calmlings — Calm Island soft 3D emotional-support mascots
summary: Verified character brand from Calm Studios: fluffy toy-like Calmlings on Calm Island posting daily soft Reels (desk scenes, wellness tips, ironic productivity fails, breathing pauses).
